nodes.summary: The parameterized $k$-Clique problem answers a bitstring $x$ and a parameter $k \in \mathbb{N}$ as follows. If $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a pair $(n, E)$ of a natural number $n$ and a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers, the answer is true exactly when there is a list of $k$ distinct natural numbers, each less than $n$, such that for any two distinct entries $u$ and $v$ of the list,…
nodes.title: Parameterized Clique

nodes.summary: A parameterized problem $P$ is fixed-parameter tractable when there is a function $D$, from pairs $(x, k)$ of a bitstring $x$ and a natural number $k$ to booleans, that is computable in FPT time and satisfies $P(x, k) = D(x, k)$ for every bitstring $x$ and every $k \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Fixed-parameter tractable problems

nodes.summary: A parameterized problem $P$ FPT-reduces to a parameterized problem $Q$ when there are a map $R$, sending each pair $(x, k)$ of a bitstring $x$ and a natural number $k$ to such a pair $R(x, k) = (x', k')$, that is computable in FPT time, and a computable function $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, such that for every bitstring $x$ and every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, $k' \le g(k)$ and $P(x, k)$ is true if and only if…
nodes.title: FPT-reductions

nodes.summary: Let $\beta$ be a type with a canonical bitstring encoding. A function $R$ from pairs $(x, k)$ of a bitstring $x$ and a natural number $k$ to $\beta$ is computable in FPT time when there are a computable function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and a polynomial-time computable function $A$ from pairs of bitstrings to $\beta$ such that $R(x, k) = A(x, 1^{f(k)})$ for every bitstring $x$ and every $k \in \mathbb{N}$,…
nodes.title: FPT time

nodes.summary: A parameterized problem is a function that assigns a boolean answer to every pair of a bitstring (a finite list of booleans) $x$ and a natural-number parameter $k$.
nodes.title: Parameterized problems

nodes.summary: Write $W[t]$ for the $t$-th level of the W-hierarchy. The parameterized $k$-Clique problem lies in $W[1]$, and every parameterized problem in $W[1]$ has an FPT-reduction to it. Every fixed-parameter tractable parameterized problem lies in $W[1]$. For every $t \in \mathbb{N}$, $W[t] \subseteq W[t + 1]$.
nodes.title: Parameterized complexity: FPT and W(1)-completeness of Clique

nodes.summary: For a list $C = (g_0, \dots, g_{m-1})$ of gates encoded as (kind, references) pairs, the list of depths is $(d_0, \dots, d_{m-1})$, where $d_j$ is computed from $d_0, \dots, d_{j-1}$ as follows. Write $g_j = (c, r)$. If $c = 0$ or $c = 1$ (an input or constant gate), then $d_j = 0$; otherwise $d_j$ is one plus the maximum of $d_a$ over the entries $a$ of $r$, where $d_a$ is read as $0$ for $a \ge j$ and the maximum…
nodes.title: Depths of the gates of an encoded circuit

nodes.summary: Let $C = (g_0, \dots, g_{m-1})$ be a list of gates encoded as (kind, references) pairs and let $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ be a list of booleans. The gate values of $C$ under $a$ are the values $(v_0, \dots, v_{m-1})$ of the flat Boolean circuit on $n$ inputs obtained by decoding each $g_j$ to a gate on $n$ inputs, evaluated at the assignment that gives input $i$ the value $a_i$.
nodes.title: Gate values of an encoded circuit

nodes.summary: For a list $C = (g_0, \dots, g_{m-1})$ of gates encoded as (kind, references) pairs, the list of wefts is $(w_0, \dots, w_{m-1})$, where $w_j$ is computed from $w_0, \dots, w_{j-1}$ as follows. Write $g_j = (c, r)$. The weft $w_j$ is $1$ if $c = 3$ or $c = 4$ (an AND or OR gate) and $r$ has more than $2$ entries, and $0$ otherwise, plus, when $c = 2$, $c = 3$ or $c = 4$, the maximum of $w_a$ over the entries $a$ of…
nodes.title: Wefts of the gates of an encoded circuit

nodes.summary: Let $d = (d_0, d_1, \dots)$ be a list of natural numbers (the depths of earlier gates), where $d_a$ is read as $0$ when $a$ is out of range, and let $(c, r)$ be a gate encoded as a (kind, references) pair. Its depth is $0$ if $c = 0$ or $c = 1$ (an input or constant gate), and otherwise one plus the maximum of $d_a$ over the entries $a$ of $r$, the maximum over no entries being $0$.
nodes.title: Depth of one encoded gate

nodes.summary: The predecessor list of an encoded gate $(k, r)$ is $r$ when $k$ is $2$, $3$ or $4$ (a NOT, AND or OR gate), and the empty list for every other kind.
nodes.title: Predecessors of an encoded gate

nodes.summary: Given a list $w$ of wefts of earlier gates, where $w_a$ reads as $0$ when $a$ is not a position of $w$, the weft of an encoded gate $(k, r)$ is $1$ if it is a large AND or OR gate ($k \in \{3, 4\}$ and $r$ has more than $2$ entries) and $0$ otherwise, plus the maximum of $w_a$ over the entries $a$ of its predecessor list (the maximum over an empty list is $0$). In particular, input and constant gates have weft $0$.
nodes.title: Weft of an encoded gate

nodes.summary: An encoded gate is a pair $(k, r)$ of a natural number $k$, its kind, and a list $r$ of natural numbers, its references.
nodes.title: Encoded gates for weighted circuit satisfiability

nodes.summary: A list $C = (g_0, \dots, g_{m-1})$ of encoded gates is well-formed when every NOT, AND or OR gate references only strictly earlier gates: for every $j < m$ such that $g_j = (k, r)$ has kind $k \in \{2, 3, 4\}$, every entry $a$ of $r$ satisfies $a < j$.
nodes.title: Well-formed encoded circuits

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $t$ and $d$, weighted circuit satisfiability is the parameterized problem that, on a bitstring $x$ and a parameter $k$, answers true exactly when $x$ decodes to a pair $(n, C)$ of a natural number $n$ and a list $C$ of encoded gates such that: every NOT, AND or OR gate of $C$ references only strictly earlier gates; every gate of $C$ has weft at most $t$ and depth at most $d$; and there is an…
nodes.title: Weighted circuit satisfiability with bounded weft and depth

nodes.summary: For a natural number $t$, $\mathrm{W}[t]$ is the set of parameterized problems $P$ for which there is a natural number $d$ such that $P$ FPT-reduces to weighted circuit satisfiability for circuits of weft at most $t$ and depth at most $d$.
nodes.title: The level $\mathrm{W}(t)$ of the W-hierarchy

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
